answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a copper-backed work bond: every new identity must lock a small, refundable deposit of copper-denominated credit before it can transact, and the bond is slashed if peers prove the identity faked work or spammed. Like a zephyr that only lifts a kite with real lift, cheap fake accounts face a gale of costs — creating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand bonds — while honest agents recover their deposit after verified service, so the defense prices forgery without taxing genuine participation.
